$comment: The mobile device roster and the lanes that run it (#890 W0). This file is the DECLARATION; scripts/lint-e2e-wiring.mjs derives the reality from the shipped workflow YAML and the shipped suite runners and fails when the two disagree. That direction matters: three separate journeys were once committed, linted, and named in tests/matrix.json as evidence while nothing executed them, and every one of those was invisible precisely because the roster lived only in people's heads. Adding a row here does not schedule anything — wiring a lane does; a row that claims `scheduled` without a lane is a hard failure.

$status.scheduled: A lane runs it and the ledger may cite it. The normal state.
$status.promoting: New signal, staging per D3: runs on non-blocking lanes only, for `nights` scheduled nights from `since`, then is promoted to `scheduled` or deleted. It may NEVER gate a PR while promoting, and a `scheduled` flow may never be demoted here to get a lane green — that is the quarantine D3 distinguishes itself from.
$status.exploratory: A human drives it by hand; NO lane may run it. A lane running an exploratory flow makes it load-bearing without anyone deciding that, so the linter refuses it.

$doctrine: The roster SHRINKS, not fans out (E-device-only). A simulator minute on macOS costs roughly 600x a vitest second on Linux, so a claim any lower tier can falsify does not belong here at all: state variety lives in tests/integration-mobile/, pure logic in the package unit tiers, and RN accessibility/responder semantics in the @centraid/mobile-rn Vitest project. Before adding a row, name the OS fact it needs a real device to observe. If you cannot, you have found a test for a cheaper tier.

pr-gate-android.why: Device signal BEFORE merge, on the primary surface. Android per D1: Linux + /dev/kvm, and the stabler of the two Maestro drivers. The only blocking mobile device lane there is.

canary-android.why: The full roster on every merge to main, so a regression is attributable to ONE commit rather than a night's worth. Also prebuilds the native shell and gradle build directory the PR gate restores from, which is what keeps that gate inside twelve minutes.

nightly-android.why: Depth on the gating platform. Same roster as the canary; what it adds is a run against a tree nobody just pushed to, which is where a time-dependent or accumulated-state failure shows up.

nightly-ios.why: iOS release coverage — native depth plus every scheduled app-level journey, all against the iOS Release artifact. Pair once and reuse the paired profile; run-ios-depth-suite.mjs is the authoritative 18-flow list and its suite budget is bounded below the 140-minute macOS job timeout.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/pairing-can.claim: The shared prerequisite of every other journey: the gateway mints a ticket, the device is booted with the app installed, and pairing completes to Home — in under five minutes, before anything fans out.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/home-loads..claim: Ticket-only onboarding renders on a cleared client. Deliberately NARROW: it does not pair and does not reach Home, which is why #890 W0 moved the U1-mobile first-run gate off it and onto pairing-canary.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/native-v0-r.claim: Every native cover opens from Home, Settings loads, the app survives a process restart, and on Android an offline write reconnects and syncs. The one airplane-mode journey the device owns; the rest of the state grid is tests/integration-mobile/'s.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/cold-start..claim: Per-launch cold start to Home-ready, median and p95, on the release artifact with the frame-probe flag compiled in.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/scroll-fram.claim: Dropped-frame percentage during a driven scroll on the Photos grid and the People directory, sampled by the release build's own rAF sampler.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/volume-proo.claim: The native replica holds up across twenty relaunches on a volume vault.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/places-seat.claim: The Places shelf, the native map and the pin readout render over real geo_lat/geo_lng rows.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/photos-perm.claim: A REFUSED camera-roll authorization produces the app's denied takeover on an EMPTY vault — the one state in which a fabricated grid would be indistinguishable from a working one. The refusal is the OS's, which is what makes it device-only.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/photos-libr.claim: The Photos temporal library and zoom drill-down render real replica rows on the native grid.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/photos-view.claim: Viewer paging and the capability menu respond to real gestures on the native surface.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/photos-sear.claim: Grouped search reaches the viewer over the device's own FTS read.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/photos-sele.claim: Selection trash and restore round-trip as a real write through the device replica.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/docs-drive..claim: The Docs cover opens, a row's quick actions appear, and a band tap POPS rather than pushes — a React Navigation stack fact both outcomes would otherwise render identically.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/agenda-week.claim: Day and Schedule differ by the size of the read, not by fixture: the widened read carries an event two days out, and a created event appears in it.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/notes-libra.claim: The row and its body preview are two separate replica reads joined on device, and a quick capture survives a real process death.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/tasks-board.claim: The rows the phone's replica hands the screen are the vault's rows and land in the group the screen draws, and a created task appears in its group.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/people-rost.claim: The People roster renders real party rows on the origin seat.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/tally-deriv.claim: Read-time figures are derived on device, and the seat offers no verb it cannot fire.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/locker-gate.claim: Home's launcher never read the one app it must not (a WITHHELD count, never 0), and no Locker session crossed a real process boundary. Only killing the process proves the second half.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/sharing-inv.claim: The phone mints an invitation from the one subject it may share, the sheet that mints it opens, the surface that redeems one loads, and on Android the verb is WITHHELD with its own sentence while the gateway is out of reach. Named three times in tests/matrix.json as an evidence owner while nothing ran it, until #890 W0 scheduled it on the roster lanes.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/op-sqlite-p.claim: A burst of five writes, each read back before the next, ALL survive process death on real flash. The Node boot-condition tier proves 52 of 56 cells against NodeSqliteDriver — an in-memory node:sqlite stand-in with no database file and no WAL to recover — so this is the only evidence in the repo about the engine the product actually ships. NOT a concurrency claim: Maestro drives one device serially and awaits each chunk's exit, so the writes cannot overlap the reads, and an earlier draft that claimed contention was wrong. NOT an exactly-once proof either: it detects an intent RE-EXECUTED on recovery (the row would sort ahead) but not a row duplicated verbatim, which needs a surface publishing a count.
tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/op-sqlite-p.promotionNote: Ten nights because the claim is about recovery of a repeatedly-appended WAL, which is the shape that fails intermittently or not at all. Three nights would not distinguish a real fix from a lucky week.

tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/share-inten.claim: A text share delivered from OUTSIDE the app (ACTION_SEND via the activity manager) opens Quick capture carrying the shared text verbatim. The payload half is the claim: ShareIntentIngest routes through centraid://capture?text=<encoded>, so a build that opened the right screen while mangling the text is a regression a screen-only assertion misses. Android only — iOS needs a second app to share from, which the lane does not install.
tests/agent-e2e-mobile/flows/share-inten.promotionNote: Five nights: the act is deterministic once the intent lands, so the risk being staged is harness flakiness (intent timing against the ShareIntentIngest `ready` guard) rather than product nondeterminism.
